comments.value:
In a platform where everything is user generated, we don't really want to have slop on the community labs and it can be easily spammed>

This is a must.

People say, vote with your wallet.

People who do not like an aspect of something will avoid it. Some do and want it. That's their choice.

In this case, people will vote with their visits. If they don't like something, they don't want to see it. Just like seeing the same ad on TV/Youtube over and over again, you're less interested in the product/concept each time.

If your world/avatar is created with that aspect, those people will avoid you, and others who do, will enjoy. It's as simple as that.

But, in the event the masses prefer to not accept an aspect, and prefer to avoid it, they will, and the creator will have less foot traffic.

Some creators are going through means to hide these aspects to get people to join, yet people will leave as soon as they join. Wasting people's times, further annoying them, more complaints come up, and less people willing to world hop due to additional wasted effort.

I've been in small groups of world hoppers, AI worlds tend to get maybe 5-10minutes of time before someone drops down another portal and everyone forgets.

Good Creators are honest with what they use for their worlds. Listing AI should be part of that. And I applaud those point out where they used AI. I know of at least one (it's my home world, and the AI use case isn't effecting the world directly, but for an information panel).

Personally, I'd be more willing, not so much the same level as a non-ai touched, to visit the world if the creator is honest and up front.

AI has been over used in places where a human, a skilled human, should have done it. As someone who works in IT, I see thousands of others in IT and media creation losing their jobs, because someone wanted to save a few dollars, at the cost of quality. Ford is rehiring staff because of how AI has damaged their quality and wasted so much time and money.

This filter helps reduce these nuance headaches. Just like "Hide This Avatar Globally" would, hiding that Avatar ID no matter who wore the avatar.

Just like using a websearch, we can add a - before a word, to force-exclude those listings, say I want pictures of animals, but exclude elephants. "Animals -elephants". As we currently sit, we cannot tag/classify something as AI-Used to begin filtering it out.

Refusing to flag a world as created "with AI", speaking over all, should be seen as on par with not flagging a world Jump Scare/Gore or Adult Content.

As a practical matter, this will not work.

Most world creators rely on external assets from platforms like BOOTH. Furthermore, for programming elements like Udon and shaders, the use of AI coding assistants has become commonplace. Unless the original creators of these assets explicitly disclose AI usage, it is impossible for the world creator to detect it.

In short, placing the entire burden of verification and disclosure solely on the final world creator is structurally unrealistic.
I'd love to have this option! I am very anti-ai and even if you're not, we should at least have the right to choose what we're exposed to! Please consider this type of toggle! thank you
Yes please. I desperately want to filter out the garbage.

Some people here might also be interested in:

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/tackle-the-misleading-world-thumbnails-issue

i hate this AI topic, but this is more of like clickbate previews made or enhanced with AI.

also i don't mind if one single object was made by AI, the final composition should be true to the user uploading and tagged correctly

details:
With the wave of generative AI content used throughout games/platforms that run on user-generated content such as VRChat, it should be required that creators tag their avatars & worlds appropriately with "Contains Generative AI Content" when the avatar/world contains ANY generative AI assets/content.

The goal is so that users who do not wish to see such content, can filter it out through VRChat's native Content Gating system.

Screenshot below as an example.
title: Add "Contains Generative AI Content" tag to the Content Gating system
